articles.title: KOI desata la locura: Empieza la operación Ave Fénix
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Ibai estaría en serios problemas económicos, pero eso no ha evitado que sus fans mantengan la esperanza
articles.summary: Ayer saltaba una noticia durísima. Rogue, por medio de la empresa que la mantiene estaría en impagos con jugadores y streamers antes de unirse a KOI. Esto se habría mantenido al ju
articles.body: Ayer saltaba una noticia durísima. Rogue, por medio de la empresa que la mantiene estaría en impagos con jugadores y streamers antes de unirse a KOI. Esto se habría mantenido al juntarse con el equipo de Ibai Llanos, lo que ha generado muchos quebraderos de cabeza. Debido a esto, varios de los proyectos que Ibai estaba preparando no se han podido hacer, y en otros ha tenido que ser el propio streamer el que haya subsanado las deudas. Esto habría llevado a que hubiera puesto cerca de 3 millones de euros de su bolsillo. Pero ahora ha surgido un plan. Operación Ave Fénix Entre los fans de KOI ha surgido un rumor. Parece que podría estar gestándose algo gordo dentro de la organización, que llevaría a que el equipo reviviera como un fénix tras quemarse. Y esto ha sido inspirado por el propio Ibai, quien no se quiso hacer eco de la noticia de Rogue, pero publicó un twit enigmático. &quot;El mito del Ave Fénix ha seducido a diferentes civilizaciones de todo el planeta con su simbolismo de esperanza, aplomo, memoria y regeneración, un ave milagrosa que siente la muerte y la prepara con mimo y serenidad para después resurgir de sus cenizas incólume y vigorosa&quot;, se puede leer en su publicación. El mito del Ave Fénix ha seducido a diferentes civilizaciones de todo el planeta con su simbolismo de esperanza, aplomo, memoria y regeneración, un ave milagrosa que siente la muerte y la prepara con mimo y serenidad para después resurgir de sus cenizas incólume y vigorosa.? Ibai (@IbaiLlanos) August 30, 2023 Esto ha desatado la locura entre los seguidores del equipo, que esperan con ansia el momento en el que KOI resurja de sus cenizas, ya sea como el mismo equipo que es actualmente o sea en otro lugar. Ha empezado a hacerse famosa una imagen en la que se podría ver a un fénix morado, y que muchos se han puesto de foto de perfil. define esquizofrenia: pic.twitter.com/PeqYFVdMbC? FH & KOI KoldoAndaluz (@Estrefo14) August 31, 2023 Y ya no solo los fans, sino jugadores del equipo han decidido seguir con la broma del mito del ave fénix, proclamándose así la &quot;Operación Ave Fénix&quot;. No sabemos en qué terminará todo este movimiento, pero desde luego, a pesar de los problemas, KOI sigue movilizando a muchísimos seguidores.

articles.title: Riot Games dará la opción a los clubes de NA de fichar a los jugadores de The Guard y ascender a VCT
articles.standfirst: Leo Faria ha aceptado una de las principales peticiones de los fans
articles.summary: Sigue el culebrón en la VCT de Américas. La máxima liga de VALORANT del continente, una de las cuatro principales mundiales, y en la que pelea el actual campeón del mundo, Evil Gen
articles.body: Sigue el culebrón en la VCT de Américas. La máxima liga de VALORANT del continente, una de las cuatro principales mundiales, y en la que pelea el actual campeón del mundo, Evil Geniuses, debería, el año que viene, contar con 11 equipos. Pero para eso, tienen que solucionarse antes los problemas. Estos precisos problemas llegan de la mano de The Guard. El equipo que había ascendido por su propia calidad a la liga no consiguió demostrar fuera del servidor lo que Riot Games le pedía para poder formar parte de la competición. Ahora siguen tratando de solucionar el problema. La plaza es, de momento, para los jugadores El pasado sábado, Riot Games se desdecía de lo señalado una semana antes. La empresa desarrolladora de VALORANT, entre otros juegos, había decidido que los jugadores de The Guard no participarían con un undécimo equipo, pero las peticiones de la comunidad cambiaron su parecer. An update regarding the players impacted by The Guards decision to not move forward with VCT Americas 2024-25 pic.twitter.com/oLhjSJDaYy? VALORANT Esports NA (@valesports_na) September 1, 2023 Así dice el comunicado: &quot;Hoy los cinco jugadores que ganaron el Ascension 2023 de Américas con The Guard han terminado su contrato con el club. Nos hemos reunido con ellos esta tarde, y les hemos hecho saber que son libres de buscar oportunidades con una organización o como agentes libres. Tienen tiempo para buscar ser fichados por otro equipo o buscar un club válido para el puesto de ascenso. Nos morimos de ganas de verles continuar con su carrera como jugadores&quot;. After working directly with the players, reviewing the process, and giving ourselves more time to think through the problem, we&apos;ve landed on a path that gives them a chance to compete in the VCT Americas league next year. I want to thank everyone for their support of the players.... https://t.co/YKe8s4gFPY? Leo Faria (@lhfaria) September 1, 2023 Con esto, los cinco jugadores podrían ponerse de acuerdo, y de conseguir una organización, conformar la undécima plaza de la liga. Leo Faria también se ha querido pronunciar al respecto: &quot;Tras trabajar directamente con los jugadores, ver el proceso y darnos más tiempo de pensar, hemos llegado a un camino que les da la oportunidad de jugar en la VCT Américas el año que viene. Quiero dar las gracias a todos por su apoyo a los jugadores, tomamos la primera decisión muy rápido, y rápidamente nos dimos cuenta de que había sido un error, como nos demostró vuestro feedback. Me alegro de que hayamos podido arreglar este error y dejar a los jugadores jugar&quot;.

articles.title: G2 estaría planteándose fichar a los exjugadores de The Guard y hacerse con el puesto de VCT Américas
articles.standfirst: El equipo europeo emigró a NA en busca del ascenso, pero cayó estrepitósamente
articles.summary: G2 siempre está ahí. Cuando menos te lo esperas, el club de los samurais, fundado por el español Carlos &apos;Ocelote&apos; vuelve a aparecer en la actualidad, trayendo noticias fr
articles.body: G2 siempre está ahí. Cuando menos te lo esperas, el club de los samurais, fundado por el español Carlos &apos;Ocelote&apos; vuelve a aparecer en la actualidad, trayendo noticias frescas para todos los fans de los esports, da igual cuál sea la disciplina. Hace ya un año que conocíamos las franquicias de VALORANT, entre las que no entraba G2 debido al &apos;caso Ocelote&apos;. El CEO de la empresa se vio obligado a apartarse de la actividad del equipo, pero sin él tampoco les ha ido mal. Las secciones de LoL y de CS siguen ganando, y también la de VALORANT femenino, actuales campeonas del mundo. Ahora podrían tener también una alegría en la parte masculina del shooter. Un ascenso que cuesta más de lo esperado Cuando Riot hizo oficial que G2 se quedaba sin puesto en las ligas franquiciadas, todos los fans de VALORANT se llevaron las manos a la cabeza. Los ya archiconocidos vídeos de Carlos Ocelote con Andrew Tate y su falta de disculpas llevaron a que el club no se encontrara entre los elegidos. Sin embargo, la respuesta del equipo fue rápida. Se mudaron a Norte América y comenzaron a formar un gran equipo para ascender, con ShahZaM como máximo exponente. Sin embargo, no consiguieron llegar a la máxima competición. Ahora podrían conseguirlo por otro lado. Según señala Lembo, el equipo de los samurais estaría haciendo números para contratar al antiguo conjunto que luchó por The Guard y consiguió el ascenso a la VCT Américas. Eso les permitiría ocupar su puesto, y alcanzar por lo tanto la máxima competición. Por el momento no se sabe si desde Riot aceptarían su candidatura, pero podrían ser una opción más que viable.

articles.title: Briar no ha llegado al juego abierto... ¡Pero ya causa estragos en el PBE!
articles.standfirst: La campeona acaba con un enemigo sin que el jugador use el teclado
articles.summary: Briar es la nueva campeona que llegará a League of Legends. Aún no se ha podido disfrutar en abierto en la Grieta del Invocador, pero ya está disponible en el PBE. Esto permite a a
articles.body: Briar es la nueva campeona que llegará a League of Legends. Aún no se ha podido disfrutar en abierto en la Grieta del Invocador, pero ya está disponible en el PBE. Esto permite a algunos jugadores probarla antes de tiempo, y ver si está a buen nivel para entrar en el juego. En este caso parece que entrará con mucha fuerza, debido a los estragos que puede causar su ultimate. Con ella, entra en un frenesí desatado, que permite hacer daño sin necesidad de tocar ni el teclado ni el ratón... y eso puede estar muy muy roto. Una kill pulsando solo la &apos;R&apos; Eso ha pasado en el vídeo que traemos hoy. El streamer Dumbs, creador de contenido finlandés, ha podido probar a la novedad del juego. Y ha demostrado que necesita algún que otro cambio para que pueda estar al nivel del resto de campeones. En este caso, caza a una Quinn backeándose en la botlane, y gracias a su &apos;R&apos;, la alcanza antes de que esta vuelva a su base. Mientras que se realiza la interacción, y como Briar pega sola cuando está en frenesí, Dumbs comienza a correr al rededor de una mesa que tiene detrás de sí. Finalmente, la campeona acaba la pelea sola, matando a su oponente.

articles.title: Fallece DaveeyS, jugador de VALORANT en KRÜ Esports
articles.standfirst: El jugador disputó la Champions de Los Ángeles con el conjunto argentino
articles.summary: Hoy nos toca dar una de esas noticias que nunca se quieren dar. El mundo de los esports es un lugar lleno de vitalidad, y en el que lo que más destaca es la juventud de sus partici
articles.body: Hoy nos toca dar una de esas noticias que nunca se quieren dar. El mundo de los esports es un lugar lleno de vitalidad, y en el que lo que más destaca es la juventud de sus participantes. Es precisamente por eso que cuesta escribir este tipo de noticias. Santiago Galvis Ruiz, más conocido como DaveeyS ha fallecido este domingo 3 de septiembre, según ha hecho público su equipo, KRÜ Esports, tras sufrir una descompensación. Comunicado de KRÜ &quot;Es con profunda tristeza que tenemos que comunicarles que, tras sufrir una descompensación el domingo, falleció DaveeyS. No hay forma de suavizar esto, nos tomó a todos por sorpresa. Daveeys, Santi, era un player espectacular y un compañero de primera. Con su característica humildad trabajadora, se sentía orgulloso de poder inspirar y representar a su país y región en lo más alto del VALORANT mundial. Fue su sueño, y lo vio cumplido. Todos en KRÜ acompañamos en este difícil momento a su familia y amigos, y pedimos a toda la comunidad que los apoyen con su fuerza y cariño.&quot; Santiago disputó con el equipo del Kun Agüero todas las competiciones en las que han participado este año, desde el Lock In de Sao Paulo a la Champions de Los Ángeles, a la que se clasificaron mediante el LCQ. También jugó la VCT Américas, en la que fue el único jugador colombiano. MARCA Gaming quiere mandar un fuerte abrazo a toda su familia y amigos, así como a KRÜ Esports tras esta desafortunada noticia.

articles.title: Miniboo, ex jugador de CASE Esports podría jugar con Team Heretics en la VCT EMEA
articles.standfirst: El duelista pasaría así a la máxima competición continental
articles.summary: Tras la temporada, que culminó hace dos semanas con la gran final del Champions de Los Ángeles, ya han comenzado los movimientos. Todos los equipos de VCT, las competiciones más im
articles.body: Tras la temporada, que culminó hace dos semanas con la gran final del Champions de Los Ángeles, ya han comenzado los movimientos. Todos los equipos de VCT, las competiciones más importantes de VALORANT internacional, están buscando reforzarse. Uno de los primeros en cerrar un acuerdo verbal sería Team Heretics, según lo publicado por Anonimotum y Lembo, ya que se habrían hecho con los servicios MiniBoo, exjugador de CASE Esports y vigente campeón de la Rising, la primera división española. El mejor duelista de la Rising, a VCT Dominykas Lukasevicius, más conocido como MiniBoo habría conseguido un puesto en Team Heretics para la próxima VCT EMEA. El club primero negoció con CASE Esports, para después llegar a un acuerdo verbal con el jugador. Según señalan los medios antes mencionados, otros dos conjuntos habrían preguntado por el duelista, pero este habría elegido finalmente a los herejes, que tenían vacante ese puesto tras la salida de Keloqz. También estarían buscando un repuesto para AvovA, y estarían pendientes de la decisión de Mixwell.

articles.title: Ibai se moja con la situación actual de KOI: "Es absolutamente imposible que desaparezca".
articles.standfirst: El streamer ha querido hablar de su club de esports tras las últimas polémicas
articles.summary: KOI está ahora mismo en boca de todos. Tras la polémica de los impagos por parte de Infinite Reality, empresa que está por detrás de Rogue, muchos han hablado sobre cómo podría ter
articles.body: KOI está ahora mismo en boca de todos. Tras la polémica de los impagos por parte de Infinite Reality, empresa que está por detrás de Rogue, muchos han hablado sobre cómo podría terminar este problema. Se ha dicho incluso que Ibai podría salir del conjunto morado. Sin embargo, el propio Ibai comenzó hace unas semanas la &apos;Operación Fénix&apos;, un movimiento llamado a hablar de la resurrección del club de las carpas y de una clara mejora. Ahora ha hablado sobre el tema en su stream, a partir de las preguntas de un seguidor. &quot;Se vienen unos meses muy prometedores&quot; El streamer vasco se encontraba respondiendo las preguntas de sus seguidores, cuando uno de ellos le preguntó por KOI. Aunque reacio a responder, Ibai dijo lo que pudo: &quot;No puedo contar mucho sobre este tema. Diría que van a venir unos meses muy prometedores&quot;. Entiende que la situación actual no permite confiar mucho, pero ha querido dar su propia opinión: &quot;Lo que ahora estáis viendo, que todo parece drama y está mal, tengo la sensación de que todo estará bien pronto . No puedo entrar en detalles en directo, me pondría en un compromiso&quot;. Finalmente, como no podía ser de otra manera, ha hablado sobre la operación fénix y la posible desaparición de KOI: &quot;Operación Fénix, sí. He leído muchas cosas de gente que, aprovechando cosas que ha leído se hace sus propias historias, es normal. Os diría que KOI es absolutamente imposible que desaparezca&quot;.

articles.title: Best Xbox Series X/S Accessories to Buy Right Now
articles.summary: The best controllers, headsets, storage expansion, and more accessories for the Xbox Series X/S
articles.body:
The best Xbox Series X/S accessories can elevate your gaming experience from a regular good time to a deck-out setup, customized to your needs. Whether you need additional rechargeable batteries, extra controllers that pair nicely with Xbox , a great gaming headset for immersive audio, or even interchangeable thumbsticks, these accessories are all available for the taking (well, buying).

TL;DR – These Are the Best Xbox Series X/S Accessories:

KontrolFreek FPS Freek Inferno Performance Kit

Microsoft Xbox Series X/S Play & Charge Kit

While the Xbox Series X/S console and Xbox Wireless Controller can get you started on your console journey, there’s no harm in enhancing what’s already there. If you want to install more games, for instance, it doesn't hurt to expand the console's base storage. Maybe you want to you want to play with friends or kick racing games up a gear. We've even found some other controllers to get the job done well.

The best part is that you don't have to break the bank to upgrade your setup. However, for those looking to indulge a bit more, there are, of course, premium options available to truly enhance your gaming journey, even if you're just a casual Xbox Game Pass player.

The Xbox Series X comes with a standard 1TB of storage, with some of that being instantly eaten away by the operating system, leaving you with 802GB of usable space. When you consider that some Xbox Series X games are well over 100GB once installed, that space fills up quickly if you're not on top of your data management. So if you want to play the games you want when you want without worrying about having to delete and redownload, investing in an SSD for Xbox is a good idea.

The officially licensed Seagate Xbox Storage Expansion Card is a great external SSD for the Xbox Series X|S , coming in 1TB and 2TB sizes to install way more games. This drive is compact while remaining an easy plug-and-play solution that just about anyone can figure out – no tech wizardry required. Just slot the drive in the Xbox’s dedicated storage expansion port, and it should be good to go.

Since the Seagate Xbox Storage Expansion Card isn’t connecting to the console via USB and opts for a direct PCI Express link instead, it opens up a whole lot of bandwidth. In fact, the speeds are almost the same as the Xbox’s internal SSD, thanks to Xbox Velocity Architecture. Load times and latency in games should feel nearly identical to playing on the internal storage. Support for quick resume is even baked in for seamless switching between titles and getting you back into the action where you left off, all with a minimal wait time.

The only major downside to this highly capable memory card is the price. But considering the speedy 2,400 MB/s transfer speeds, optimized performance, and ease of use, it’s worth the splurge.

We wouldn’t blame you if you didn’t want to splash all your hard-earned cash on Seagate’s Xbox expansion card. If that’s the case, you might want to turn your head to the WD C50 Expansion Card, a more affordable alternative. It comes in 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB storage sizes to keep your favorite titles installed and ready to play.

This expansion card is officially licensed by Microsoft, too, so you can simply plug and play without any hassle of installing additional storage and taking your Xbox apart. Just like Seagate’s offering, this drive slots right into the Xbox’s expansion slot – no major setup required. From there, it’s easy to install the games you want, and thanks to WD C50’s portable size, it can be taken along to a friend's house to play games they haven’t installed.

Unlike the majority of other great external hard drives for Xbox, this one can install and play games straight from the drive rather than downloading them to the console. While transfers and boots might be slightly slower than the internal storage on the Xbox, the difference is hardly noticeable. Support for Xbox’s Quick Resume feature also means jumping right back into the action where you left off is quick and simple. The only time you’ll need to reboot is during game updates.

Turtle Beach Stealth 500 Headset - Photos

Combining affordability, simple connectivity, and solid sound, the Turtle Beach Stealth 500 makes for a great Xbox Series X/S gaming headset . Audio quality is the main reason you want to grab this headset. In our review of the Turtle Beach Stealth 500 , our reviewer found it delivers well-balanced and bold audio across almost all frequencies. It only really struggles with highs at higher volumes, which is expected from such a well-priced headset. Even in busy, action-packed games, sound remained easily discernible with some detailed positional audio to boot. When communicating with teammates, the microphone is serviceable but sometimes quiet.

While out-of-the-box sound on the Turtle Beach Stealth 500 headset is great, Turtle Beach offers the Swarm II mobile app to swap between a few audio presets, monitor battery life, and activate features like chat boost and Super Human Hearing. In theory, Super Human Hearing sounds like a great way to detect enemies in games, but in action, our reviewer found it detracts rather than enhances the game. For more advanced customizations, a desktop version is available where it's possible to map hotkeys, adjust sound using a 10-band EQ, and change headset settings.

The headset itself also features a series of controls to adjust settings like volume, modes, and connectivity. The button layout feels cramped and hard to distinguish, making it easy to press the wrong controls. At least, the headset is lightweight and durable with a unibody design and a stretchable strap inside the band that contorts to fit your head. The headband can’t extend, and the earcups aren’t adjustable, but even still, the lighter clamping force and plush design keep the headset comfortable on the head for hours.

Connecting the Turtle Beach Stealth 500 is a straightforward process, as the headset comes with a 2.4GHz wireless dongle for a low-latency connection to the Xbox. Bluetooth 5.2 is available for other devices. However, there’s no wired connectivity option. Luckily, the 40-hour battery life will last even the longest gaming marathons.

It’s hard to go wrong with the classic Xbox Core Controller. Sure, it’s a little basic and lacks the flash of some higher-end gamepads, but it works seamlessly with the console, sneaks in a few upgrades from previous models, and remains ultra affordable. An IGN expert reviewed the Xbox Core Controller and loves the familiar, comfortable shape that feels well-balanced in your hands. With the addition of textured grips on the side handles and triggers, the controller is easier than ever to hold firmly in your hand.

The Xbox Core Controller features all the inputs needed to excel in just about every type of game. However, the D-pad is a real standout. It’s slightly more concave than older generations, with the cardinal directions feeling more pronounced than the Xbox Elite Series 2 . Each press is clicky and responsive with surprising feedback, preventing mispresses. Games like Mortal Kombat and Midnight Suns benefit most from this improved D-pad.

Another notable design shift is the inclusion of a share button for a simpler way to take screenshots or start recording video clips. While the share button can be remapped, it has functionality limitations, and remapping controls as a whole isn’t as advanced as some gamepads. Still, it’s possible to swap the functions of a few inputs with Xbox’s easy-to-use Accessories app.

Xbox Wireless comes on the Xbox Core Controller, allowing for a simple connection to the console. A new feature called “Dynamic Latency Input” keeps latency to a minimum for fewer misspresses and a snappy experience. Given that it’s a wireless controller, battery life is a concern, and this controller keeps things rather archaic by relying on two AA batteries. A USB-C port is available for those who’d rather just skip the hassle of batteries and opt for a wired connection instead. Still, even with this slight flaw, the Xbox Core controller is the best Xbox Series X/S controller you can buy and there are plenty of colors to choose from .

Note that this is also our pick for the best PC controller

For a controller that gets all the basics nearly perfect, look no further than the Turtle Beach Recon. This inexpensive gamepad offers a layout similar to most Xbox controllers with all the traditional buttons, sticks, and triggers found on the Core Controller. In our review of the Turtle Beach Recon , we found the buttons were responsive, with only a light touch required to activate them, while the D-pad and thumbsticks kept ultra-smooth.

But what makes this controller shine is its customization options. On the backside are two mappable Quick Action buttons that can be configured to do a range of functions. That’s not all, because above the Xbox button at the front of the gamepad are additional controls. Not only can the mic and headphone volume be adjusted when a headset is connected, but four customizable modes and “Super Human Hearing” are available. “Super Human Hearing focuses on directional audio at a cost to overall sound, while the various “modes” let you change volume settings, adjust EQ, map buttons, and activate the Pro Aim Focus. Pro Aim Focus mode is particularly useful, letting you adjust the right stick’s sensitivity.

You might be wondering what’s actually sacrificed on the budget-friendly Turtle Beach Recon, and the answer is wireless connectivity. It’s exclusively wired, but the excellent performance and build quality more than make up for it. Rumble is even included, and we’re big fans of the cooling grips, ensuring the controller doesn’t slip from your hands during heated moments.

Moza R3 Racing Wheel and Pedals – Photos

Racing games, like Forza Horizon 5 and Crew Motorfest, are taken up a notch when paired with a top racing wheel , letting you feel the twists and turns of the virtual open road. One wheel that does a particularly great job of offering a realistic feel without draining your bank account in the process is the Moza R3. This Xbox-licensed wheel is a direct drive, leaving similarly priced belt- and gear-driven systems in the dust.

An IGN expert tested the Moza R3 , finding the force feedback smooth, silent, and instant, even communicating subtle feedback. Sure, it doesn’t offer the arm-shredding power of some higher-end wheels, but the 3.9Nm of peak torque still lets you feel the bumps and curves. When playing on Xbox, it’s even possible to adjust the force feedback to your liking using the Moza Racing app, delivering more oomph to lower-end feedback.

The D-shaped 280mm wheel is comfortable in hand with a polyurethane wrapping to provide a solid grip, although the finish cheapens it slightly. Still, the face is brushed metal with easy-to-access Xbox controls for breezy menu navigation, while the wheel and base come with a reliable and sturdy steel clamp to keep the setup secure. Along with the wheel comes an all-metal two-pedal set that offers good adjustability. Unfortunately, a spring with Hall effect sensors instead of the load cell is used, so breaking is a little less consistent.

If you're not a fan of any components, upgrading and swapping Moza parts is simple. The wheel base and steering wheel snap onto each other easily using a rigid quick-release system, and the pedals can be changed out (or added onto) at any time. So, even though this might be an entry-level system, when you’re ready to kick things up a gear, you won’t have to do so all at once. It’s easy to see why this is our favorite Xbox racing wheel .

Those who want to make the most out of the Xbox Series X console probably have all their favorite streaming apps installed, like Netflix, YouTube, and Disney+. It’s great that you can skip grabbing one of the best streaming devices , but it can be a pain to switch between your TV’s remote and your Xbox controller. The easiest solution is the PDP Universal Gaming Media Remote Control. This officially licensed product lets you navigate your console, apps, and TV from one handy device.

The PDP Solis Xbox Gaming Media Remote Control offers a layout similar to your average TV controller. The typical volume and channel controls, along with all the necessary media buttons, like play, pause, stop, and fast forward, are available. Each control is easy to access, so you don’t need to fumble around with the buttons on your Xbox controller attempting to figure out what should be pressed. Should you need to use some Xbox controls, the A, B, X, Y, and home buttons are on the remote, while the arrow and select keys make it simple to navigate menus.

Beyond its media and Xbox buttons, this remote offers a few handy features. The biggest plus is the motion-activated backlit buttons, meaning all you need to do is lift the remote to see the controls glow for fewer mispresses in dark spaces. Replacing batteries will never be a concern either, as the PDP Solis Xbox Gaming Media Remote Control comes with a rechargeable battery. There’s even solar charging, so juicing up via the USB-C won’t need to happen as often. But perhaps best of all, this remote control doesn’t come with a high price tag, costing under $20.

8. KontrolFreek FPS Freek Inferno Performance Kit

Competitive gamers will appreciate the upgraded precision that the KontrolFreek FPS Freek Inferno Performance Kit offers. This cheap and cheerful Xbox Series X accessory comes with a mid-rise and high-rise thumbstick to customize your gameplay. Each is made of a durable rubber material to provide additional grip and comfort for an upper hand when you need it.

With the mid-rise thumbstick installed, control and movements should be improved, while the increased height of the high-rise thumbstick can boost precision and accuracy when aiming. Less force will also be required when using the thumbsticks for easier movements in general. Just be prepared for the slightly chunkier thumbsticks to be a bit harder for those with smaller hands to master.

If you’re worried about installing the Inferno Performance Kit, don’t be. Taking apart a controller is not required, as they just snap right on top of your existing thumbsticks, completely changing your gaming experience in the process. A four-prong design keeps the thumbsticks securely in place during all the action, so you never need to worry about it falling off as you line up and take the perfect shot.

9. Microsoft Xbox Series X/S Play & Charge Kit

As mentioned, our top Xbox controller, and the one packaged with the console, the Xbox Core controller, uses AA batteries. Luckily, Xbox makes it simple to swap out those disposable ones for a more eco-friendly, rechargeable option. The Microsoft Xbox Series X/S Play & Charge Kit is a rechargeable battery pack, so you’ll never need to worry about searching the drawers, cabinets, and remotes for batteries again. It’ll probably be more economical in the long run, too.

The Play & Charge Kit can fully recharge within 4 hours, getting you back in on the action quickly. However, playing as you recharge is even possible, thanks to a USB-C cable, ensuring the battery doesn’t run out during an integral game moment. That cable is pretty long, so it should be able to reach you on the couch or chair. Even when you’re not playing, the batteries will still charge up with the Xbox in standby mode.

The amount of playtime that comes with each full charge is reported to be right around 30 hours. That’s in line with many other wireless controllers. However, the actual playtime will vary based on how you use the controller.

10. Razer Universal Quick Charging Stand

Compatible with all Xbox controllers, aside from the Xbox Elite 2, the Razer Universal Quick Charging Stand conveniently charges controllers when not in use. The controller simply mounts into the stand, coming back fully charged in about 3 hours, ready for the next gaming session. You’ll know the gamepad is charging when the indicator light at the front of the stand begins to glow.

The stand comes in a range of colors that match perfectly with the controllers. Whether you’re after a bit of flash that comes from a green or red option or would rather keep things more subdued with white or black, chances are, there’s something that suits your gaming setup. The charging stand also helps keep things looking a bit more organized, and the solid build quality means it should last just as long as your controller.

With overcharge and overheat protection, there shouldn’t be much worry about short-circuiting your controllers. Protection from accidental drops is also considered, so there’s rubber at the bottom of the stand that prevents slippage, and the controller will securely slot into place magnetically. However, the high-end design comes with a higher price tag, and a charging brick isn’t even included with the price.

New Xbox Series X/S accessories are released all the time. Whether it’s new third-party controllers, headsets, or even different color options for the accessories you already have.

However, one of the most notable upcoming Xbox accessories has to be the Elite Series 3 controller which is rumoured to release soon.

How to Pick the Best Xbox Series X/S Accessories

Choosing the best accessories for your Xbox Series X/S can really take your gaming experience to the next level. But deciding on what accessory to invest in can stump many users. Think about what you value most in gaming. Are you all about competitive play, or do you prefer immersive single-player adventures? Your gaming style will no doubt determine your accessory choices.

It goes without saying, but before making any kind of purchase, you must check that the accessory you're eyeing is compatible with your specific Xbox Series X or S model. Not all accessories work with both, so it's important to match them up correctly.

Decide on the features you want. Are you looking for extra buttons on a controller for more control, a high-quality headset for crisp audio, or a charging station to keep your gear powered up? Once you’ve made a decision, ensure you pick an accessory from a reputable brand with good user reviews.

Accidents happen, and sometimes things just don't work out as expected. Make sure to check the warranty and return policy for any Xbox accessory you buy to avoid any potential headaches down the line.

Ultimately, however, gaming is a personal experience. Choose accessories that resonate with you, as you’ll be the one using them!

This question is really dependent on your personal needs. However, some of the most essential Xbox accessories include additional storage, like the Seagate Xbox Storage Expansion Card, extra controllers, and a solid headset.

There are some great Xbox controllers available, including the Xbox Core Controller. However, if you want advanced controls, the Elite Series 2 controller and Turtle Beach Stealth Ultra are two great higher-end options. But, if you’re on a budget, you can get a plenty of capability from the Turtle Beach Recon.

You can prevent your Xbox controllers from sticking or drifting by regularly cleaning them. Avoid eating or spilling drinks near your controller, and add a controller cover to protect it.

Kegan is an avid gamer who has been playing games since his Atari days. From a young age Kegan was tinkering with PCs and now has a passion for building custom gaming computers.

It’ll probably be more economical in the long run, too.

The Play & Charge Kit can fully recharge within 4 hours, getting you back in on the action quickly. However, playing as you recharge is even possible, thanks to a USB-C cable, ensuring the battery doesn’t run out during an integral game moment. That cable is pretty long, so it should be able to reach you on the couch or chair. Even when you’re not playing, the batteries will still charge up with the Xbox in standby mode.

The amount of playtime that comes with each full charge is reported to be right around 30 hours. That’s in line with many other wireless controllers. However, the actual playtime will vary based on how you use the controller.
10. Razer Universal Quick Charging Stand

Compatible with all Xbox controllers, aside from the Xbox Elite 2, the Razer Universal Quick Charging Stand conveniently charges controllers when not in use. The controller simply mounts into the stand, coming back fully charged in about 3 hours, ready for the next gaming session. You’ll know the gamepad is charging when the indicator light at the front of the stand begins to glow.

The stand comes in a range of colors that match perfectly with the controllers. Whether you’re after a bit of flash that comes from a green or red option or would rather keep things more subdued with white or black, chances are, there’s something that suits your gaming setup. The charging stand also helps keep things looking a bit more organized, and the solid build quality means it should last just as long as your controller.

With overcharge and overheat protection, there shouldn’t be much worry about short-circuiting your controllers. Protection from accidental drops is also considered, so there’s rubber at the bottom of the stand that prevents slippage, and the controller will securely slot into place magnetically. However, the high-end design comes with a higher price tag, and a charging brick isn’t even included with the price.
New Xbox Series X/S accessories are released all the time. Whether it’s new third-party controllers, headsets, or even different color options for the accessories you already have.
However, one of the most notable upcoming Xbox accessories has to be the Elite Series 3 controller which is rumoured to release soon.
How to Pick the Best Xbox Series X/S Accessories

Choosing the best accessories for your Xbox Series X/S can really take your gaming experience to the next level. But deciding on what accessory to invest in can stump many users. Think about what you value most in gaming. Are you all about competitive play, or do you prefer immersive single-player adventures? Your gaming style will no doubt determine your accessory choices.

It goes without saying, but before making any kind of purchase, you must check that the accessory you're eyeing is compatible with your specific Xbox Series X or S model. Not all accessories work with both, so it's important to match them up correctly.

Decide on the features you want. Are you looking for extra buttons on a controller for more control, a high-quality headset for crisp audio, or a charging station to keep your gear powered up? Once you’ve made a decision, ensure you pick an accessory from a reputable brand with good user reviews.

Accidents happen, and sometimes things just don't work out as expected. Make sure to check the warranty and return policy for any Xbox accessory you buy to avoid any potential headaches down the line.
Ultimately, however, gaming is a personal experience. Choose accessories that resonate with you, as you’ll be the one using them!

This question is really dependent on your personal needs. However, some of the most essential Xbox accessories include additional storage, like the Seagate Xbox Storage Expansion Card, extra controllers, and a solid headset.

There are some great Xbox controllers available, including the Xbox Core Controller. However, if you want advanced controls, the Elite Series 2 controller and Turtle Beach Stealth Ultra are two great higher-end options. But, if you’re on a budget, you can get a plenty of capability from the Turtle Beach Recon.
You can prevent your Xbox controllers from sticking or drifting by regularly cleaning them. Avoid eating or spilling drinks near your controller, and add a controller cover to protect it.
Kegan is an avid gamer who has been playing games since his Atari days. From a young age Kegan was tinkering with PCs and now has a passion for building custom gaming computers.

articles.title: The Best PC Cases for Gaming in 2026
articles.summary: The best PC cases will keep your gaming PC organized and stylish. Looking to upgrade or build a new PC? Check out our favorite cases!
articles.body:
Whether you’re focused on grabbing the best graphics card or busy deciding between an AMD or Intel processor, both will be useless unless you’ve got a solid case to house your gaming PC build. Our favorite case is the ultra-spacious Corsair Obsidian 1000D , but from top-notch cable management and sleek designs to compact and budget options, we’ve found a great PC case for gaming that's bound to fit your needs.

TL;DR - These Are The Best PC Cases for Gaming:

PC cases might be overlooked more than other components when building your rig. But cases are your gaming PC’s home, and features like cable management, airflow, and ventilation can make or break your rig. Of course, you also want to show off all your gaming hardware, so finding a PC case with a large window is a must. Perhaps most importantly, you need your build to fit in the case. So, we’ve taken all of that into consideration, bringing six of the best PC cases for gaming.

With room for an E-ATX motherboard, two of the best power supplies (PSU), and 18 fans, the Corsair Obsidian 1000D proves that sometimes, bigger is better.

Speaking of doubling up, the Corsair Obsidian 1000D can fit an E-ATX motherboard, and a mini-ITX motherboard at the same time, letting you build two PCs into one, without the need for dual-booting.

OK, so everyone might not need two of everything, but with its humongous size, and impressive cable management capabilities, the Corsair Obsidian 1000D is by far one of the best choices, capable of making an efficient and frankly stunning gaming PC, now you just need to figure out where this goliath of a case can live.

If you’re looking to build a budget gaming PC, you might want to consider a more affordable PC case. The MSI Mag Forge 112R is a more affordable option that still offers plenty of room to work with, and comes bundled with four ARGB fans and a controller capable of powering more of the best PC fans .

The MSI Mag Forge 112R is listed as an ATX case, but just about has room (and mounting holes) for an E-ATX motherboard, giving you plenty of room to work with, and allowing plenty of room for bigger graphics cards, such as the GeForce RTX 4090 , which requires a lot of space.

The only downsides to the MSI Mag Forge 112R are the lack of front-panel USB 3.2 Type-C, and its poor options for solid cable management, but then again, at such an incredible price, you can’t expect everything to be perfect.

While most people tend to lean toward an ATX case, there’s a lot to be said for buying a larger E-ATX PC case. The Thermaltake Core P8 is a massive PC case that offers ample room to work with and space for up to an impressive eighteen 120mm fans, making it one of the best PC cases for airflow .

The Thermaltake Core P8’s most unique feature though is its modular design, which lets you take the entire case apart and rebuild it to your liking, making it one of the most heavily modifiable gaming PC cases on the market today.

If you’re worried about losing space to this monster of a PC case, the good news is, the Thermaltake Core P8 is also wall mountable, saving you space and making it the centerpiece of your gaming setup.

Building an all-white gaming PC can quickly become expensive, but if you’re going to go through that added expense, you might as well go with a case that performs as great as it looks.

The Corsair iCUE 7000X RGB offers plenty of space, as well as offering impressive cable management, helping with airflow, and making sure your gaming PC always looks incredible.

Not only does the Corsair iCUE 7000X RGB come with four pre-installed SP140 RGB fans, it also includes an iCUE Commander Core XT, letting you add two more RGB fans, and temperature sensors.

Sometimes bigger isn’t better, especially when you are limited on space. The Razer Tomahawk Mini-ITX is one of the best Mini-ITX cases on the market, thanks to its solid build quality and stylish minimalist design.

Thanks to Razer Chroma RGB lighting effects, the underside of this case looks amazing, and can easily be customized with the Razer Chroma app to match the rest of your gaming setup.

While Micro-ITX cases can often be difficult to work with due to their restrictive size, the Razer Tomahawk Mini-ITX is surprisingly easy to work with and also includes easy-to-use built-in cable management.

HYTE is a relative newcomer to the gaming hardware scene, but don’t let that put you off. The HYTE Y60 is a stunning PC case with a bold new design. You can choose between black, white, and red to set off your build, and despite looking truly beautiful, the HYTE Y60 is near-on perfect for cable management.

Not only can you mount your GPU vertically, the Y60 comes with an included PCIe 4.0 cable, cleanly framing your graphics card. It also fits just about any of the best motherboards . Thanks to its unique design, you can easily tuck unsightly cables behind the back panel, allowing you, your friends, and viewers (if you like to stream) to marvel at the work of art your PC can become with this case.

There’s plenty of CPU cooler support and room for fans, too, meaning your build will stay cool. Route your cables through the floor of the case, and hide connections from plain sight in this aesthetically pleasing case that is guaranteed to draw some heat (but not the bad kind).

When it comes to picking the best gaming PC cases, we look beyond just how good they look. Yes, a PC case should look great, it’s the centerpiece of your gaming setup, but it also needs to have optimal airflow and be built to last.

With that in mind, we look for cases that offer plenty of room for airflow, including checking dust filtration to ensure that it doesn’t cause any issues with intake.

Size is also an important factor we take into account, with modern GPUs growing in size, and taking up more bays, it’s important to ensure that your new case can accommodate modern GPUs.

Finally, we check the quality of the components used in the case, has the case been built to last, does it feature an innovative design that assists you with the best cable management possible, and whether it’s easy to build in.

When considering what parts will affect the FPS you get in game, sadly most people ignore their PC case. Heat is one of your biggest enemies when it comes to building a gaming PC and if your case doesn’t have good airflow, you will soon find your custom rig throttling to maintain safe temperatures, which in turn will reduce FPS.

Not always, there are obviously some safety concerns around having an open case, especially for those with pets or young children. An open case can also lead to dust building up inside the PC quickly.

That being said, some PC cases, such as the Thermaltake Core P8 rock an optional open design, which can help increase airflow and improve performance, so if it’s safe to do so, there are no issues with having an open case.

Should bottom fans be intake or exhaust?

The fans at the bottom of your PC case should be intake, as should the fans on the front panel of your case. The fans on the back of your case, next to your IO panel, and also the fans at the top should be expelling hot air.

The simple way to think about this is that hot air rises, so it should always come in from the bottom and be exhausted from the top.

Kegan is an avid gamer who has been playing games since his Atari days. From a young age Kegan was tinkering with PCs and now has a passion for building custom gaming computers.

articles.title: Best Budget Gaming Keyboards in 2026
articles.summary: Not everyone can afford expensive peripherals, so here are our picks for the best budget gaming keyboards.
articles.body:
Budget keyboards have massively improved over the past few years. There are now some great mechanical and membrane options with many of the same features as high-end boards from a few years ago. That makes it a great time to swap from an old, tired keyboard to a proper gaming board that can provide a small competitive edge – and make your gaming time much more comfortable.

TL;DR – These Are the Best Budget Gaming Keyboards:

Many budget gaming keyboards come with plenty of features, like programmable keys, RGB lighting, onboard controls, and so on. Sure, you might have to downsize a little or sacrifice a few fancy features, but you can also find the best gaming keyboard to compliment your existing gaming PC setup.

The SteelSeries Apex 3 TKL is proof that a gaming keyboard doesn’t have to be expensive to keep up. This $45 option already ticks a lot of things off the list including being water- and dust-resistant, silent switches ideal for late-night gaming, and it even has adjustable feet for your gaming comfort. Also, apart from its dedicated media keys, it’s also fully macro-programmable, which makes it an excellent budget choice for RPG, MMO, and MOBA gamers.

That’s not all; this feature-rich keyboard includes three-way cable management built-in and eight customizable RGB lighting zones. Simply put, it’s packed with great features and delivers a solid performance you wouldn’t expect from a sub-$50 keyboard. Plus, if you like this in a full-sized version, the SteelSeries Apex 3 comes with pretty much the same features.

The Gamakay TK75HE V2 is a feature-rich mechanical gaming keyboard with Hall Effect switches. Unlike regular mechanical switches, these are analogue, so you can adjust how far down you need to press to trigger an input, enable rapid trigger mode to aid responsiveness and even improve your movement mechanics with SOCD. Polling rates can be set up to 8000Hz wired, while 2.4GHz wireless and Bluetooth connectivity adds flexibility for use with other devices.

Beyond these FPS-focused features, the TK75HE V2 is just a great keyboard to use, with a convenient and compact 75% layout, an integrated volume wheel in the top right and a miniature LCD display in the bottom right. The typing experience is surprisingly good for a keyboard at this sub-$80 price point, and the Magnetic Phoenix switches we recommend are quite quiet for a mechanical keyboard too. Overall, a great value option that is amongst the best available from a smaller keyboard brand.

The Logitech K845 is unlike any gaming keyboard you’ve ever seen. In fact, Logitech has taken great lengths to prove that a gaming keyboard can look just as sleek and as elegant as the best keyboards for productivity. Make no mistake, though; this mechanical keyboard is just as excellent for gaming as it is for typing up emails and documents. As long as you’re not seeking tournament-level performance, that is.

You even have your pick of mechanical switches, so you can get the one that feels most comfortable and satisfying to you. It’s a bit minimalist on features, with just five lighting patterns on hand for backlighting and no macro recording. However, it’s an excellent budget keyboard if you need one to see you through all your computing needs, including casual gaming. Plus, for a sub-$60 option, you’re getting a robust option that’s rated for up to 50 million clicks.

The RGB lighting on the Roccat Magma might overwhelm you. Or, you might absolutely love it. The 5-zone, 10-LED RGBA backlighting doesn’t just light up the symbols on the keys; it makes the whole keyboard deck glow beautifully. Of course, it doesn’t just look good; it performs beautifully as well. Its keys aren’t just quiet, due to its silent membrane switches; they’re also reasonably responsive for gaming.

Of course, its Roccat Easy-Shift[+] button duplicator, which gives you a second set of functions on the WASD zone, might help with your gaming performance as well. That’s a lot of premium features on a gaming keyboard that’s now under $50. It even has a detachable palm rest, which to be honest is nothing to write home about, but it adds to its value.

The Keychron V3 is a budget gaming keyboard that is suitable for gamers, programmers, and casual users. It’s compatible with Windows, Mac, and Linux, featuring a TKL design with 87 keys. Despite its wired connection, the keyboard is portable thanks to its compact size.

This affordable gaming keyboard offers QMK/VIA support, allowing you to change keymaps on your keyboard without installing any software on your PC. Fully customizable from top to bottom, the Keychron V3 offers hot-swappable support so you can change out your switches to almost any 3-pin or 5-pin MX mechanical switches available. The double-shot PBT keycaps extend the durability of this keyboard while keeping the price down, and feel comfortable no matter if you’re firing spells in an RPG, or switching weapons in a shooter.

Before you start your search for a budget gaming keyboard, you need to set a max price you’re willing to spend. Many great affordable options are available for $100 or less, and you’ll even find some reliable keyboards for under $50 – just don’t expect loads of gaming features. But, no matter what, you don’t need to worry about this great gaming accessory being a big expense.

After you decide on your budget, you need to select your design. Do you want full-size, TKL, or something even more compact? TKL and compact boards like 75%, 65% and 60% are better for those who want to have plenty of mousing space or play on a small desk, while full-size is best for those who need a num pad or tons of extra keys. You also need to determine if you want wired or wireless connectivity. Wired options are cheaper, but wireless keyboards can add some extra flexibility and a cleaner look – though having to recharge them can be annoying.

The switch type is equally important. Membrane switches are made of the same stuff as buttons on a TV remote, so they harden over time and don't deliver much tactile feedback, nor are they customisable with new keycaps. However, they are generally the cheapest option and they tend to be quiet, too. Mechanical switches deliver a significantly better feel that doesn't degrade over time, with more customisation options and a galaxy of different varieties that can feel heavy or light; clicky, tactile or linear, and loud or quiet.

Additional features are what make your keyboard and gaming keyboard. Is per-key RGB lighting a must? Do you need fully programmable macro keys for RPG, MMO, and MOBA games? How about n-key rollover to ensure you can press multiple keys simultaneously? Most gaming keyboards will have most of these features nowadays, but it's worth checking to make sure that the keyboard you're considering has all of the bells and whistles that you think are essential.

Keyboard and Mouse vs. Controller for Gaming

The biggest – and most obvious – difference between the best PC controllers and a gaming keyboard and mouse combo is the physical design of the peripherals. A great controller rests in your hands, putting all the inputs in an easy-to-reach location, making it ergonomic and simple to use. Its buttons and triggers are also often remappable. A keyboard and gaming mouse combo is larger and more spread out, requiring you to use a gaming desk or lapdesk when playing. However, you get an excess of possible inputs at your fingertips, and oftentimes, each key and button is customizable.

Where a keyboard and mouse pairing often pulls ahead of controllers is in precision and responsiveness, so most will turn to this trusty combo when playing competitive FPS. But the analog sticks on a gamepad deliver smoother control over certian movements, which is a boon in racing games. Modern controllers even offer haptic feedback for a more immersive gaming experience.

Still, whichever input device you choose, it’s more a matter of personal preference than anything else. While playing the best PC games with a comfortable controller might seem sacrilege to an accuracy-focused keyboard and mouse enthusiast, you just need to do you.

Yes, the best wireless keyboards can be just as good for gaming as their wired counterparts, depending on the type of connection available. You’ll want to grab a keyboard offering a dedicated 2.4GHz wireless dongle for a reliable, speedy link to your gaming PC. That type of connection, especially in the best high-end gaming keyboards , usually offers similar latency to wired keyboards. Replacing or recharging batteries is necessary, but luckily, most wireless keyboards last weeks or months as long as RGB lighting is disabled. Plus, you no longer need to deal with a pesky wire.

Is an expensive gaming keyboard worth it?

Whether you splurge on a gaming keyboard depends on how often you play and if you do it competitively. For those who occasionally game after school or work, you’ll get by just fine with our budget-friendly picks. However, avid gamers, especially in those in competitive genres, can benefit from higher-quality switches and keycaps, more customization, and advanced features provided by magnetic switches. You’ll also see higher polling rates and additional features bring an edge over opponents. But the average gamer will get by without all these frills, saving a few bucks.

Will is deputy tech editor for IGN, specialising in PC hardware, sim racing and display tech. He has been publishing about games and technology since 2001 (age 12). Will was formerly Deputy Editor at Digital Foundry. He is currently playing BattleTech (2018) with the BattleTech Advanced Universe mod.

After you decide on your budget, you need to select your design. Do you want full-size, TKL, or something even more compact? TKL and compact boards like 75%, 65% and 60% are better for those who want to have plenty of mousing space or play on a small desk, while full-size is best for those who need a num pad or tons of extra keys. You also need to determine if you want wired or wireless connectivity. Wired options are cheaper, but wireless keyboards can add some extra flexibility and a cleaner look – though having to recharge them can be annoying.

The switch type is equally important. Membrane switches are made of the same stuff as buttons on a TV remote, so they harden over time and don't deliver much tactile feedback, nor are they customisable with new keycaps. However, they are generally the cheapest option and they tend to be quiet, too. Mechanical switches deliver a significantly better feel that doesn't degrade over time, with more customisation options and a galaxy of different varieties that can feel heavy or light; clicky, tactile or linear, and loud or quiet.

Additional features are what make your keyboard and gaming keyboard. Is per-key RGB lighting a must? Do you need fully programmable macro keys for RPG, MMO, and MOBA games? How about n-key rollover to ensure you can press multiple keys simultaneously? Most gaming keyboards will have most of these features nowadays, but it's worth checking to make sure that the keyboard you're considering has all of the bells and whistles that you think are essential.
Keyboard and Mouse vs. Controller for Gaming

The biggest – and most obvious – difference between the best PC controllers and a gaming keyboard and mouse combo is the physical design of the peripherals. A great controller rests in your hands, putting all the inputs in an easy-to-reach location, making it ergonomic and simple to use. Its buttons and triggers are also often remappable. A keyboard and gaming mouse combo is larger and more spread out, requiring you to use a gaming desk or lapdesk when playing. However, you get an excess of possible inputs at your fingertips, and oftentimes, each key and button is customizable.

Where a keyboard and mouse pairing often pulls ahead of controllers is in precision and responsiveness, so most will turn to this trusty combo when playing competitive FPS. But the analog sticks on a gamepad deliver smoother control over certian movements, which is a boon in racing games. Modern controllers even offer haptic feedback for a more immersive gaming experience.

Still, whichever input device you choose, it’s more a matter of personal preference than anything else. While playing the best PC games with a comfortable controller might seem sacrilege to an accuracy-focused keyboard and mouse enthusiast, you just need to do you.

Yes, the best wireless keyboards can be just as good for gaming as their wired counterparts, depending on the type of connection available. You’ll want to grab a keyboard offering a dedicated 2.4GHz wireless dongle for a reliable, speedy link to your gaming PC. That type of connection, especially in the best high-end gaming keyboards , usually offers similar latency to wired keyboards. Replacing or recharging batteries is necessary, but luckily, most wireless keyboards last weeks or months as long as RGB lighting is disabled. Plus, you no longer need to deal with a pesky wire.
Is an expensive gaming keyboard worth it?

Whether you splurge on a gaming keyboard depends on how often you play and if you do it competitively. For those who occasionally game after school or work, you’ll get by just fine with our budget-friendly picks. However, avid gamers, especially in those in competitive genres, can benefit from higher-quality switches and keycaps, more customization, and advanced features provided by magnetic switches. You’ll also see higher polling rates and additional features bring an edge over opponents. But the average gamer will get by without all these frills, saving a few bucks.

Will is deputy tech editor for IGN, specialising in PC hardware, sim racing and display tech. He has been publishing about games and technology since 2001 (age 12). Will was formerly Deputy Editor at Digital Foundry. He is currently playing BattleTech (2018) with the BattleTech Advanced Universe mod.

The story features a rich cast made up of both real historical figures and fictional ones, and the politics of it all can be tricky to untangle. Luckily, we've got you covered. Let's meet the characters of Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2. Be warned that these bios contain some spoilers from the first game!
articles.body:
You don't need to have played the original Kingdom Come: Deliverance to get up to speed with the sequel, thanks to an extended intro that fills you in on the broader details. But it might help to know a bit about the main cast before you set off into the medieval Bohemian countryside. The story features a rich cast made up of both real historical figures and fictional ones, and the politics of it all can be tricky to untangle. Luckily, we've got you covered. Let's meet the characters of Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2.

Be warned that these bios contain some spoilers from the first game!

Wenceslaus IV and Sigismund of Hungary: A Clash of Kings

In 1378, 25 years before the events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance, the emperor Charles IV, who was widely regarded as a pretty cool guy, died. As is often the case when a really cool king or emperor dies, this led to an inconvenient series of events. His son Wenceslaus became his successor to the throne of Bohemia, and gained a reputation for spending his days doing sod all, not showing much interest in his kingly responsibilities.

In response to this, his younger half-brother, Sigismund of Hungary, decided to make a play for the Bohemian throne and took Wenceslaus prisoner. During the events of the first game, he is seen riding around demanding the loyalty of local nobles and burning down villages he believes are harboring rebels – including Skalitz, the hometown of our protagonist, Henry.

In real life, it was a complicated situation with no clear good guys and bad guys, necessarily. I mean, if you ask me, pretty much all medieval nobles were bad guys. But in the context of KCD, Wenceslaus is the good and true king and Sigismund is the plunderous pretender. That's how Henry sees it, anyway. And if the guy on one side of a civil war had burned down my village and killed my parents, I'd probably agree.

As an additional fun fact, the real-life Sigismund founded the chivalric Order of the Dragon. You may have heard of it, since a certain Romanian prince, Vlad Dracul, was nicknamed such for being a member of it. His son, Dracula ("son of the dragon"), would go on to be even more famous.

The protagonist of both Kingdom Come: Deliverance games is a common lad named Henry who saw his whole life go up in flames and his family murdered. The son of a blacksmith, he was forced to make his way in the world without many useful skills to speak of – the very picture of a level-one RPG character. But steadily, over the course of the first game, he became a capable swordsman, a daring adventurer, and even learned to read and write – which was a rare enough skill in the middle ages, even among the nobles, that it was practically a superpower.

Henry becomes involved with a faction of nobles who oppose Sigismund and want to see Wenceslaus restored to the Bohemian throne, rising from his lowly status to be a trusted and valued retainer. He also spends some time as a monk. It's kind of a long story. But he also has a more specific quest: retrieving the stolen sword he and his father made for their lord, Radzig Kobyla, before the village was attacked.

This is the jerk who stole said sword. A Hungarian noble and supporter of Sigismund, he was the main antagonist of the first game and managed to wriggle free from the good guys' grasp by exchanging some hostages. While Henry certainly feels a sense of duty to Wenceslaus, his more personal motivation is getting that dang sword back from Toth. And then probably giving it back, pointy end first, if we're being honest. His whereabouts are currently unknown.

The Lord of Skalitz before its destruction, Sir Radzig is part of the pro-Wenceslaus faction, which is why Sigismund saw his seat of power ransacked. Also – last warning for spoilers – he's Henry's real, biological father. Which sort of makes Henry nobility. Or at least, there is a nobleman with a very strong interest in his future and wellbeing. Martin the blacksmith is still definitely Henry's father figure. But Sir Radzig has become a very important man in his life.

Sir Hans Capon is a young nobleman about Henry's age and a member of Wenceslaus' faction who plays a much larger role in KCD2 than he did in the first game, being Henry's main compatriot. They're not always the best of friends, though. Hans is a bit of a playboy nepo baby who was raised with the proverbial silver spoon in his mouth and tends to act petulant and entitled, often to Henry's frustration. He's also quite easily distracted by women.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 - Gamescom 2024 Screenshots

At the start of KCD2, Henry and Hans have been dispatched on a mission to feel out which of the remaining Bohemian nobles might be willing to stand up against Sigismund and help restore Wenceslaus to the throne. And while he's not entirely apathetic to politics, he mostly looks at this as an opportunity for travel and adventure. To be blunt, he's a bit of a dick. But he seems to have a good heart, even if he doesn't normally let it guide him. Can we fix him? That remains to be seen.

Theresa: The Girl Who Saved Your Sorry Butt

A fellow refugee from Skalitz who now lives with her uncle, Theresa is a bold woman who has saved Henry's life more than once. She's also the potential main love interest in KCD1, if you choose to pursue her side quests. It's not clear what role, if any, she will play in KCD2. But especially considering she and Henry were likely to have become romantically involved, I would be somewhat surprised if we've already seen the last of her.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 - First Screenshots

Sir Divish: The Guy Who Saved Your Sorry Butt

Sir Divish is the Lord of Talmberg, where Henry took refuge right after the destruction of Skalitz. The fortress was later seized in an intrigue orchestrated by Toth, and the climax of the first game involves a siege to reclaim it. He is, along with Radzig, one of the main conspirators of the Wenceslaus faction, and a very shrewd leader who has kept his people safe by holding his allegiances close to his chest.

Markvart von Aulitz: Probably The Real Final Bad Guy

If I'm being honest, I don't give Istvan Toth long to live. The fact that we didn't get to stick it to him at the end of the first game was a huge tease, and he only made it out by the skin of his teeth. Markvart is a bit higher up the food chain, as one of Sigismund's main army commanders and the man who led the attack on Skalitz. He was a somewhat distant enemy in the first game, seeming almost untouchable. But if I had to place my bets on who we'll be crossing swords with at the end of KCD2? I think it's probably this guy.

That should give you a pretty good idea of which important pieces are on the board at the start of this new adventure. For more, stay tuned all December long as our exclusive IGN First coverage of Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 continues.

articles.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 Review - IGN
articles.summary: An action-packed medieval saga fit for a Hollywood blockbuster.
articles.body:
Some days I’ve moped about how I'll never get back the feeling I had the first time I played Skyrim. And then Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 arrived on a mighty steed to sweep me off my feet at full gallop. Armed with excellent, skill-focused melee combat and a rousing, action-packed medieval saga fit for a Hollywood blockbuster, it's one part sequel and one part coronation, bringing a lot of the original's ideas to fruition in the same way The Witcher 3 did for CD Projekt Red or Greedfall did for Spiders. No game of this scope and scale is without some technical scuff, of course, and its competing design goals are occasionally at war with themselves just as much as our hero Henry is internally. But even still, its majesty is hard to deny.

This tragic tale picks up almost immediately where Kingdom Come: Deliverance left off back in 2018, though I don't necessarily think you need to have played the first one to get up to speed thanks to the main plot being relatively easy to follow and most of the callbacks being well explained as they happen. Henry, a blacksmith's son turned unlikely warrior, is thrown into the middle of dynastic politicking and bloodshed played out by a diverse and complex cast, including your boisterous failson of a liege lord and some truly memorable entrances from real historical figures I don't want to spoil.

The star that shines brightest across this expanse of countryside, though, is the city of Kuttenberg. I can't speak about this place in any terms less flattering than to say it might be one of the wonders of the modern RPG world. I don't think I've ever walked the streets of a virtual medieval city that feels this huge, detailed, and most importantly, alive.

The layout is based largely on the actual town that still stands today, with parts of it following the modern street grid almost exactly. It's a wonderful place to simply wander around and discover all kinds of urban adventures – from resolving a dispute between two rival sword schools to hunting down a grisly serial killer. Yes, some of the NPCs obviously share the same voice actor and others share the same face – even important side characters, which can be particularly jarring. But it’s hard to get too hung up on that in a place like this. When I first arrived here I was already more than 40 hours into my 120-hour journey, and I spent multiple in-game days gleefully shopping for the sickest duds and best armor I could afford. And that's what arriving in a huge regional capital should make me want to do!

The quest variety is what impressed me most of all, and that extends beyond just Kuttenburg. Very rarely are you simply sent to kill some bandits or carry a package to the next town – at least without some kind of interesting twist, moment of emotional turmoil, or decision built in. There are around 100 quests in total and, having done nearly all of them, practically every single one was memorable enough that it would stand out as a highlight in a lesser RPG.

Admittedly, some were slightly better in concept than execution. There was one I stumbled onto completely by accident that took me deep underground and turned my sword-swinging adventure into a horror movie, but ended up being far too short for the dread to really set in. All the same, I never felt like doing side quests ever became a chore, because I knew each one would be its own little complete episode of The Adventures of Henry, stuffed with quality writing and unique objectives. It's a testament to how consistently strong they were that 120 hours did not feel way too long to me.

Along the way are expansive, breathtakingly beautiful landscapes spread over two open-world maps, both of which are chock full of meticulously researched details of late medieval Bohemian life. There isn't a ton of variety in terms of geography – it's all wooded hills and meadows, for the most part. But that’s what the region looks like in real life. It's big enough to get lost in, and the contrast between villages and open wilderness varies things up nicely enough. I did find it odd that you can't go into most of the churches, though, since those would be near the top of my list if I were planning a tourist trip through 1400s Europe.

If the side quests are like episodes of a TV show, the main quest is a big-screen war movie that pulls out all the stops in its ambition, dialogue, and emotional range. Parts of it made me cheer. Parts of it actually brought me to tears. And Henry's ultimate nemesis got under my skin in a way video game bad guys rarely do, making me rethink everything I’d done up to that point in what might be one of the most memorable final encounters I've ever played through. It's mature without being edgy, it drips with historical authenticity, and it has interesting questions to ask you about what it means to be a hero or a villain.

It's somewhat unfortunate, then, that Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is both a mostly linear medieval action-drama and an open-world sandbox, and those two concepts don't always play well together. I'm going to skirt around spoilers the best I can, but I need to give a specific example of the worst experience I had. I need to tell you about the Hungarian Camp.

In one of the late-game areas, there is a military camp set up by King Sigismund, the evil conquering bastard you've been opposing since the first hour of the first game. I, of course, tried to assault it by myself the second I got there, and was immediately put down like a dog. Fair enough. But for the next 40 hours of adventuring, I was plotting my revenge. A fire was lit in me – motivation to become as much of a badass as possible. I studied with all of the best blademasters. I learned the way of the bow. I saved up for the best armor. I forged, by hand, the very best sword in Bohemia. Next time I showed up at that camp, things were going to be different.

So, near the end, I went back to the Hungarian Camp Rambo-style and I killed everyone there. Okay, not the cook or the tailor. And not Musa – Musa's cool. But probably somewhere in the neighborhood of 30 to 40 armed men. This was an empowering and gleeful rush, with difficult combat that tested all of my skills like never before. A real highlight of the entire journey. And these are enemy soldiers, let me remind you! I don't feel like this was an unpredictable or degenerate thing to do.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 Gameplay Screenshots

So it was a downer when, shortly after, I was asked to infiltrate this same camp as a spy, and Henry didn't even so much as mention that he had completely desolated the place and had a bounty on his head so large that the authorities would skip fines and prison and straight-up execute you if you're caught. This is a required story quest with no alternate path, so the ridiculous, frustrating solution was to sneak up on the unkillable quest NPCs several times to talk to them and start the next cutscene before that same NPC spotted me and went running to call the guards.

It also ruined my near-perfect reputation because I guess killing invading enemy soldiers was a crime the peasants Sigismund is actively oppressing couldn't forgive, and everyone in every town ended up hating me. But this was a major outlier in what was otherwise a hugely engrossing, marathon-length playthrough.

Other than that one total debacle though, I truly adored almost every minute I spent with Henry and company. The tactical, skill-based sword combat is a sharp refinement of the already great system from the first game, though I felt like at higher levels, the balance of pure stats to player skill skewed too much in favor of the former. You could probably reach the credits without actually getting particularly good at the swordplay, which was certainly not the case in the first one. But it is cleaner, more varied, and smoother to play. Archery, in particular, has improved a lot.

There's a blacksmithing minigame now, which I found a little bit clunky and unsatisfying, but it's still great to be able to use a sword I made myself in combat. And alchemy has been made way more intuitive.

I also really like the new perk system, where every level up feels like it gives you multiple choices between meaningful bonuses. In the first one, a lot of perks honestly felt more like side-grades than upgrades. There was a perk that made it so sleeping outside was more restful, but sleeping in a bed, less so. The sequel’s version only has the upside, and not the drawback, which is important if I'm going to spend my hard-earned skill points on something rather than picking it as a character background at the beginning. And while there wasn't a single quest as interesting or different as the monk arc from the original, getting to level up my scholarship and unlock new quest resolutions by destroying my enemies with facts and logic was also great.

Did I mention that it runs really well on my 4070 Ti, even at 4K and very high settings? I still can't even run the first Kingdom Come: Deliverance at max settings on this same machine, and that game is seven years old at this point. So the optimization work that was done here deserves a shout. There are also plenty of bugs, but most of them are of the silly sort you screenshot to show your friends that you'd expect in an RPG with this much ambition. Only rarely did something actually disrupt my gameplay.
